scenario.title: The Disrupted Library Reading
scenario.description: The local community library is hosting an afternoon reading of a new children's book. A pipe bursts flooding part of the library, causing minor damage but disrupting the reading event. The library staff must quickly decide how to proceed.
scenario.speaker1_persona: Raj is a calm, thoughtful individual who is good at making quick decisions in difficult situations. He is empathetic and considerate.
scenario.speaker2_persona_1: High EQ - Olivia is flexible, resourceful and able to stay calm in a crisis. She is good at thinking on her feet and considering various options before making a decision.
scenario.speaker2_persona_2: Low EQ - Olivia is easily flustered and tends to panic in stressful situations. She struggles to think clearly and make decisions when things go wrong.
scenario.speaker2_persona_3: Low EQ - Olivia is overly critical and pessimistic. She tends to see problems as insurmountable, and she struggles to find solutions in difficult situations.

conversation.speaker: speaker1
conversation.text: Oh gosh, this is a mess. We've got to figure out how to handle this quickly.

conversation.speaker: speaker2
conversation.text: Right, the children are upset. Do we cancel the event or...?

conversation.speaker: speaker1
conversation.text: No, let's not cancel. We can move to the other side of the library—the one that's not affected by the flooding.

conversation.speaker: speaker2
conversation.text: Good idea, I'll start moving chairs there. And what about the ruined books, should we start cleaning up?

conversation.speaker: speaker1
conversation.text: Yes, but first let's ensure everyone's safe. The cleanup can wait until the reading is over.

conversation.speaker: speaker2
conversation.text: You're absolutely right, safety first. I'll make an announcement and start moving people. Let's do this.
